steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Spray two 24-cup mini muffin tins with cooking spray.
Place wonton wrappers into the prepared muffin cups; press gently into the bottom and up the sides.
Bake in the preheated oven for 5 minutes. Remove from the oven and let cool in the pans.
Meanwhile, mix sausage, Monterey Jack, Cheddar, ranch dressing, and olives together in a medium bowl. Divide mixture evenly among cooled wonton cups.
Return to the oven and bake, watching closely to ensure wontons do not burn, until filling is bubbly and slightly brown, 10 to 15 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Wonton Wrapper Appetizers
raw_recipe.description: These sausage wontons are the perfect appetizer! Crispy wonton cups are loaded with cheese, sausage, olives, and ranch for a burst of flavor in every bite.

review.reviewBody: This is an elegant, easy appetizer. Some tips: DEFINITELY cook and crumble the sausage first. If you do that, you won't have to worry about making sure the sausage is cooked properly without burning the wontons. Also, leave out the olives and ranch dressing and add finely diced red pepper AND onion. I think the ranch dressing doesn't fit this recipe. You could also use an Italian 6-Blend cheese in place of the other cheeses. With all these changes, they will taste like mini sausage sandwiches, which everyone loves. Thanks!

I’ve been making these for a friend’s annual holiday gathering for at least 10 years. I keep the mixture as-is but without olives (and as others have said, cook and drain the sausage first!). For the first several years I made the cups as in the recipe but it always bugged me that the bottom of the cups never got crispy. For a couple years I made little pockets with the wonton wrappers, misted with oil and air fried which was nice. This year I went all out and made mini egg rolls and deep fried them, then re-heated in the air fryer at the party. They are so good! I serve them with buffalo sauce.

I have made this recipe with hot pork sausage, and pepper jack cheese, I also have made it in regular muffin cups, froze them after cooking, reheated them and added scrambled eggs for a delicious handheld breakfast treat.

Made these as a Thanksgiving appetizer. They were awesome! I browned turkey sausage with the herbs, pepper, onion, etc.(not the cheeses or ranch). When done, I let the mixture cool, then added the cheeses and an envelope of dry Ranch dressing . Instead of making them in won ton wrappers, I put the filling in frozen puff pastry cups to avoid a special trip to the over crowded grocers. When I ran out of those, I put the filling into wheat tortillas (flour), rolled them up and cut them into bite sized pieces. Everyone gobbled them up. Do not know how anyone could call these disgusting. My family is used to eating gourmet apps and they loved these. Will def be making again!

Loved the idea of baking instead of frying the won ton. I used Italian sausage, browned well and added a mixture of shredded mozzarella and cheddar (left out the Ranch dressing). Rather than putting in muffin tins, just filled then wonton and folded into triangles. Be sure to moisten edges with a little water to seal, then bake. We were pleasantly surprised how very good they were. Freeze the extras, just heat in moderate oven for a quick snack.

I make these but with a little difference. First of all, I brown the meat first, and drain it well. I would think the wontons would be full of grease if not browning first, and not totally done making the sausage gummy as one reviewer said. I also add an extra 1/2 cup of each cheese. Instead of the ranch dressing, I add 2 cups sour cream and a packet of Hidden Valley Dressing mix..adding the sour cream after removing from the heat. After filling, they only need to be baked for 5-8 mins. I'm surprised 15 mins doesn't totally burn the edges of the wontons. made these for christmas day and they were a bit hit

After draining the cooked sausage, I add a quarter each, finely chopped green and red, bell peppers, with some sliced green onion instead of the olives. I use pepper jack cheese and cheddar, and finish following the recipe. I use non stick pans, so I don't need to spray the pans. Always a crowd-pleaser!

I followed the suggestions of Chris Miller Catley. I cooked the wontons 6 minutes until they were browning at the edges. I then cooked the sausage, added some diced red pepper and onion, left out the ranch dressing and olives. Then filling the cups could refrigerate until guests arrived. Popped them in the microwave and the guest raved over the appetizer. It was a hit for the evening. Thank you Chris Miller Cately for your review!!!!

This is a great appetizer! You can take liberties with this recipe. I added 1/2 C of red peppers and 1/2 C of mushrooms both chopped. I also added some jalapeños to the non kid ones for a nice kick! I used mozarella instead of cheddar cheese. I did cook the sausage first and that worked out great, and the ranch dressing it calls for wasn't too much in my opinion. I will make these again!

I have made this many, many times and it has always been a hit with my relatives. The first time I made it, I couldn't find won ton wrappers so I substituted with Phyllo cups. Worked perfectly and you don't have to pre-bake the cups.

This was a yummy appetizer and so easily adaptable as many reviewers have noted! I made half the recipe using 1/2 pound turkey sausage (daughter doesn’t eat pork) seasoned with 1/2 tsp Italian Seasoning. I precooked the sausage. I added 1 cup shredded Italian cheese blend, 1/4 each finely diced red bell pepper (1 mini pepper does the trick) and onion. I pre-baked shells 5 minutes, filled them, and popped them in the oven once I arrived at the party. Thank you- so easy!

My family loves these little appetizers and ask for them whenever we have a party. Definitely cook and drain the sausage first. I can't even imagine how they would turn out if you failed to do that. Will be making these again this Christmas season!
I have been making this app for years and it is always one of the first to be gobbled up!

I used to make these when I worked in an office and they were so loved, that when we had a potluck, my contribution was filled in by others as Deb's Amazing Wontons. I read some of the older comments and can't believe that some called these "gross". I also saw some variations that I will try, such as pepperjack cheese and a lower-fat meat. I will use mushrooms to make a vegetarian wonton.

These little dudes always hit when I make them. They are good reheated or cold. Ppl love them and always ask me if I’m making them. I add a little vegetable oil to my wraps before cooking them the first time it helps! YES, cook the sausage before adding it to all the other ingredients. make sure it is thoroughly cooked! It is meat y’all come on now. I also add a little extra cheese on top before they go back into the oven after being assembled. You can’t go wrong with this little bites of yummy!! Cook them with love and I promise they will taste even better. 🤍🤍 good luck!

This the BEST appetizer ever! The best way is to bake your wrappers and they can be stored in a ziplock baggie for whenever you want to use them. Then just fry the sausage, add the cheese and ranch and fill the wonton wrappers and bake in oven (or microwave) for a very short time until cheese is melted. Whenever I make these they disappear instantly.

Make this for Church coffee hour every so often. Have never brought any home. Wish I had the hint on the shot glass sooner. Million dollar suggestion. Makes the process so much faster & easier. Thank you & God Bless

This is my go to when needing an appetizer (I’m actually making them right now). My friends and family request this recipe anytime we have a get together. Over the years I have tried different ways of making it. I’ve used Italian sausage and different types of breakfast sausage. This morning I am using maple sausage and wondered how scrambled eggs might be in it. I’ve never had a mini baking cup pan so I make them the regular cupcake size using 1 wonton wrapper. Recently I decided to use the mixture and make egg rolls. Of course it was fantastic! There are so many tweaks you can do to this recipe to make it your own or just try new variations. I’m not an olive fan so that is something you will never find in mine. Love this recipe.
Mixed cheddar and mozzarella together as well as the Monterey Jack.
